question: In busy clinics, what usually leads to unsafe injection practices?

options.A: Lack of basic electricity in rural health posts
options.B: Patient preference for expensive oral medications
options.C: Shortage of qualified medical doctors on duty
options.D: High patient volumes leading to rushed procedures

explanation: When clinics are overcrowded and nurses have heavy workloads, it is easy to feel rushed and skip important safety steps. Always take a deep breath and prioritize safety, no matter how busy the shift gets! [learn more](GNS122_U3_T4#GNS122_U3_T4_h1)

question: Why do many patients prefer getting an injection instead of taking oral drugs?

options.A: Injections are universally cheaper than tablets at pharmacies
options.B: Patients believe injections work much faster than oral drugs
options.C: Government insurance policies only cover parenteral treatments
options.D: Oral medications are strictly forbidden for common tropical fevers

explanation: Many patients feel that injections bring quicker healing compared to pills. As nurses, patient education is our tool to explain how both forms work safely! [learn more](GNS122_U3_T4#GNS122_U3_T4_h1)

question: Which virus mostly attacks the liver and often leads to a long-term (chronic) infection?
explanation: Hepatitis C loves liver cells (hepatocytes)! Once it gets in, it can stick around for a long time causing chronic liver issues. Great job remembering your hepatitis facts! [learn more](GNS122_U3_T4#GNS122_U3_T4_h2)

question: How do blood-borne viruses bypass skin defenses during a faulty injection?

options.A: By neutralizing normal skin flora using toxic viral enzymes
options.B: By utilizing direct mechanical inoculation into the vascular system
options.C: Through active transport via superficial sweat gland ducts
options.D: Through airborne droplet inhalation during needle preparation

explanation: Think of a hollow needle like a tiny doorway that physically punches right through the skin, dropping germs straight into the bloodstream or deep tissues. This is why safe technique is everything! [learn more](GNS122_U3_T4#GNS122_U3_T4_h2)

question: What long-term liver damage is strongly linked to chronic viral hepatitis?
explanation: When the liver fights chronic inflammation over time, it gets scarred. This severe scarring is known as cirrhosis. You've got this! [learn more](GNS122_U3_T4#GNS122_U3_T4_h3)

question: Which action during drug administration puts nurses at the highest risk of a needle-stick injury?

options.B: Transporting sealed vials on a clean stainless tray
options.C: Swabbing the injection site with methylated spirit
options.D: Recapping used needles after medication administration

explanation: Trying to put the cap back on a used needle is one of the commonest ways nurses accidentally prick themselves. Never recap used needles—just drop them straight into the safety box! [learn more](GNS122_U3_T4#GNS122_U3_T4_h3)

question: Which germ is most commonly found in localized skin abscesses caused by unsterile injections?
explanation: Staph aureus lives happily on our skin, but if it gets pushed deep into tissues by an unsterile needle, it forms painful pus-filled abscesses. Good thing we always practice proper antisepsis! [learn more](GNS122_U3_T4#GNS122_U3_T4_h4)

question: A patient comes in with a warm, painful, swollen lump on the buttock two weeks after getting an injection at a local chemist. What is the most likely issue?
explanation: A warm, swollen, fluid-filled lump right where an injection was given points straight to an abscess. You are learning to spot clinical clues like a pro! [learn more](GNS122_U3_T4#GNS122_U3_T4_h4)

question: Which major nerve is in the greatest danger if a gluteal injection is given incorrectly?
explanation: The sciatic nerve runs right through the gluteal region. Knowing your anatomical landmarks protects your patients from nerve injury. Keep revising those landmarks! [learn more](GNS122_U3_T4#GNS122_U3_T4_h5)

question: What happens when an irritating drug is accidentally injected straight into an artery instead of a vein or muscle?

options.A: Severe local ischemia and tissue necrosis
options.C: Rapid systemic clearance by renal excretion
options.D: Immediate neutralization of the drug by platelets

explanation: An accidental arterial injection causes blood vessels to clamp shut, cutting off blood supply and damaging the tissues downstream. Careful aspiration before injecting saves lives! [learn more](GNS122_U3_T4#GNS122_U3_T4_h5)

question: Why is it important to take a detailed injection history during a patient assessment?

options.A: To assess the patient's personal preference for oral drugs
options.B: To pinpoint the timing and setting of potential exposure events
options.C: To determine the patient's exact blood clotting factor levels
options.D: To calculate the exact financial cost of previous treatments

explanation: Knowing where and when a risky procedure happened helps you and the medical team figure out what screening tests the patient might need. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T4#GNS122_U3_T4_h6)

question: Which of these is NOT typically seen in a localized injection site complication?

options.A: Generalized skin rash across the trunk
options.B: Visible fluctuant swelling with purulent drainage
options.D: Distal neurological deficits like foot drop

explanation: A rash all over the trunk is usually an allergic or systemic sign, whereas injection site issues stay local to the spot where the needle went in. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T4#GNS122_U3_T4_h6)

question: What is the standard nursing and medical care for a mature, pus-filled injection site abscess?

options.A: Assisting with surgical incision and drainage
options.C: Massaging the mass vigorously to disperse the fluid
options.D: Applying cold ice packs to reduce localized swelling

explanation: When an abscess is full of pus, medication alone isn't enough—it needs to be drained so the tissue can heal properly. You'll see this often in surgical postings! [learn more](GNS122_U3_T4#GNS122_U3_T4_h7)

question: Why is emotional and psychological support so important for patients with chronic viral infections?

options.A: Psychological therapy prevents all forms of peripheral neuropathy
options.B: Emotional support replaces the need for costly antiviral medications
options.C: Counseling directly accelerates the regeneration of damaged hepatocytes
options.D: Patients often face severe stigma and emotional distress upon diagnosis

explanation: Getting a lifelong diagnosis can feel very heavy, and social stigma makes it harder. As nurses, our warm, non-judgmental ears bring so much comfort to our patients. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T4#GNS122_U3_T4_h7)

question: Where is the best place to keep sharps disposal containers in a treatment room?

options.A: Inside a locked storage cabinet in the hallway
options.B: At arm's length right near the point of use
options.C: On the floor near the facility exit door
options.D: Underneath the main administrative nurse desk

explanation: Keep sharps bins close by! When you don't have to walk across the room carrying a used needle, accidents are much less likely to happen. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T4#GNS122_U3_T4_h8)

question: What is the most effective way to stop unsafe injection practices in primary care clinics?

options.A: Requiring all patients to purchase their own reusable glass syringes
options.B: Replacing all clinical nurses with automated medication dispensing robots
options.C: Banning all forms of intramuscular injections in rural health posts
options.D: Enforcing strict no-recapping policies and ensuring reliable sharps container supply

explanation: System safety works best when management provides enough safety boxes and enforces clear rules like 'never recap your needles.' Excellent work finishing this set! [learn more](GNS122_U3_T4#GNS122_U3_T4_h8)
